title: Drop the expanded loan guarantee for small firms
name: Drop the expanded loan guarantee for small firms
headline: Drop the loan guarantee. Saves £0.2bn in 2029-30.
description: The Budget expands the Growth Guarantee Scheme to back £6.5 billion more lending to smaller firms this Parliament, with longer loans. Switch this on to drop the expansion.

baselinePolicy.text: The Growth Guarantee Scheme supports £6.5 billion of additional SME lending between 2026-27 and 2029-30 (Table 6.1 line 75).

source.quote: It supports an additional £6.5 billion of lending between 2026-27 and 2029-30

alreadyIncludes: The Growth Guarantee Scheme supports £6.5 billion of additional SME lending between 2026-27 and 2029-30 (Table 6.1 line 75).

lines.title: British Business Bank: Expand the Growth Guarantee Scheme to support £6.5 billion of additional SME lending across this Parliament

rawSource.note: Reversal on the spending side: the Treasury’s costing with the sign kept (a line that reduced borrowing is spending the reversal adds back; a line that cost money is spending the reversal saves).

caveats: The Treasury’s costing is on the OBR October 2026 forecast, the baseline used here. Effects before the start year are not applied: 2026-27 falls before any Budget of yours.

considerations.text: The Treasury’s scorecard figure is the certified direct costing for the measure, including the behavioural response the Treasury and OBR agreed; the Budget 2026 policy costings document gives the method.
